TRACKED-CHANGES REDLINE
Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper
Matter: contracts work — Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Engagement: contracts/banking/account-control-agreement-counterparty-paper-review/scenario-01

Instrusted changes key: [ADD] = insertion required; [DELETE] = deletion of counterparty language required; [RESTORE] = reinstatement of firm-standard/base provision required; [REJECT] = counterparty deviation removed; [CONCEDE] = counterparty change accepted per controlling client instruction.

This redline reconciles the counterparty's markup against the base deal materials, the internal account control agreement playbook, the executed credit agreement, the depository bank's standard form, the account details, and the deal-team correspondence/checklists (LCA Matter File 6, Counterparty Markup 32, Schedules and Exhibits 84, Deal Correspondence 110). Misfiled administrative correspondence (doc 58) is from an unrelated engagement and has NOT been relied on.

WAIVER AND SCOPE. Consistent with the controlling partner instruction (doc 110), the client concedes the indemnification basket conversion but treats any survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. This redline implements that posture.

--------------------------------------------------
REDLINE — SECTION BY SECTION
--------------------------------------------------

SECTION 2 — DEFINITIONS

2.1 "Material Adverse Effect"
[DELETE][REJECT] Delete the counterparty's newly added carve-outs that exclude from "Material Adverse Effect" any adverse change, event, development, or state of facts arising out of or resulting from (a) any regulatory action, inquiry, investigation, or enforcement proceeding or (b) the existence or pendency of any regulatory inquiry or request for information.

[ADD][RESTORE] Restore the firm-standard "Material Adverse Effect" definition without a blanket regulatory-action carve-out. In accordance with Schedule 3.7, which discloses two pending regulatory inquiries, the definition must carve out only Regulatory Actions that (i) are taken by a governmental authority in its ordinary, non-discriminatory enforcement of law against the industry generally, (ii) did not arise out of, and are not attributable to, the facts or circumstances underlying the pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7, and (iii) do not, individually or in the aggregate, result in a material adverse effect that is the subject of any pending inquiry. By rejecting the blanket carve-out, the two pending regulatory inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7 remain within the scope of "Material Adverse Effect" and any resulting adverse change is not excluded.

SECTION 8 — INDEMNIFICATION

8.2 Indemnification Cap.
[DELETE][REJECT] Delete the counterparty's silent reduction of the indemnification cap.
[ADD][RESTORE] Restore the indemnification cap to the level required by the internal playbook and the executed credit agreement. The cap is not subject to negotiation because reducing it would undermine the risk allocation that the depository bank's standard form and the executed credit agreement reflect.

8.3 Indemnification Basket.
[CONCEDE] ACCEPT the counterparty's conversion of the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket. Per the controlling deal-team instruction (doc 110), the client has conceded the basket conversion. No redline mark is required against this conversion; the provision is accepted as marked by the counterparty.

8.4 Retained Liabilities.
[ADD][RESTORE] Preserve the retained-liability carve-outs reflected in Schedule 5.2. The counterparty's indemnification changes (cap reduction and basket conversion) would otherwise operate to silently shift the retained liabilities listed in Schedule 5.2 to the indemnitor. Add express language confirming that the retained liabilities identified in Schedule 5.2 are excluded in all events and are not subject to, and do not count toward, the indemnification basket. [RESTORE] the schedule-defined scope so that the retained liabilities remain the sole responsibility of the party retaining them.

SECTION 12 — REPRESENTATIONS; SURVIVAL

12.3 Survival of Representations and Warranties.
[REJECT][RESTORE] Delete the new, shortened limitation period for the survival of the core representations and warranties and restore the full survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B. The counterparty's new limitation period directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix. Per the controlling deal-team instruction (doc 110), ANY survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue. The full survival periods in Exhibit B (including the survival of the fundamental/core representations, the Schedule 3.7 regulatory-inquiry representations, and the indemnification obligations) must be retained without reduction.

--------------------------------------------------
COMPLIANCE AND GENERAL INSERTIONS
--------------------------------------------------

[ADD] Governing-law and consent-to-jurisdiction provisions to be conformed to the depository bank's standard form and the executed credit agreement, as reflected in the base matter file.

[ADD] Confirmatory assignment/control provisions as required by the depository bank's standard form (UCC control arrangement) so that the account control agreement operates as a perfected control agreement over the relevant deposit account as contemplated by the executed credit agreement.

[ADD] Integration clause: this agreement, together with the executed credit agreement, the account details, and the schedules and exhibits, constitutes the entire agreement of the parties and supersedes all prior correspondence and checklists.

--------------------------------------------------
CERTIFICATION OF REDLINE
--------------------------------------------------
This redline is certified to incorporate every required modification and insertion identified by reconciling the Counterparty Markup (doc 32) against the base Deal Materials (doc 6), the Schedules and Exhibits (doc 84), and the controlling Deal Correspondence (doc 110). The three counterparty deviations (indemnification cap reduction, MAE regulatory-action carve-outs, and survival-period shortening) are each addressed as marked above. Basket conversion is conceded per client instruction. Misfiled administrative correspondence (doc 58) was disregarded.

args.body:
ISSUES / RISK MEMORANDUM
Review of Account Control Agreement — Counterparty Paper
Matter: contracts work — Review Account Control Agreement Counterparty Paper
Engagement: contracts/banking/account-control-agreement-counterparty-paper-review/scenario-01

PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT

I. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

We have reviewed the counterparty's markup of the Account Control Agreement (the "Agreement") against (i) the internal account control agreement playbook, (ii) the executed credit agreement, (iii) the depository bank's standard form, (iv) the account details, and (v) the related correspondence and checklists. The counterparty accepts most firm-standard provisions but has introduced three deviations: (1) the indemnification cap is silently reduced and the indemnification basket is converted from a deductible to a tipping basket; (2) the definition of "Material Adverse Effect" ("MAE") adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter; and (3) a new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

Pursuant to the controlling deal-team instruction (Deal Correspondence doc 110), the client will concede the basket conversion but treats ANY survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue. Accordingly, we recommend: (a) accepting the basket conversion (conceded); (b) rejecting the indemnification cap reduction; (c) rejecting the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs; and (d) rejecting the survival-period reduction as a walk-away issue and restoring the full Exhibit B survival matrix.

The misfiled administrative file (doc 58) concerns an unrelated engagement and was not relied on for this analysis.

II. DEVIATION ANALYSIS

----------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 1: Indemnification Cap Reduction and Basket Conversion
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Section references: Sections 8.2 (Indemnification Cap) and 8.3 (Indemnification Basket); Schedule 5.2 (Retained Liabilities).

Counterparty markup action: The counterparty silently reduces the indemnification cap and converts the basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.

Playbook requirement: The internal playbook and the executed credit agreement require (i) an indemnification cap set at the firm-standard level (as reflected in the base matter file and the depository bank's standard form) and (ii) an indemnification basket structured as a deductible, such that the indemnitor is only liable for losses in excess of the basket threshold.

Risk rating: HIGH (cap reduction); MEDIUM (basket conversion, but conceded per client instruction).

Exposure analysis: A reduced cap directly limits the aggregate indemnity available to the client and would operate, together with the basket changes, to silently shift the retained liabilities listed in Schedule 5.2 onto the indemnitor. Because Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities intersect the indemnification provisions the markup alters, the scheduled exceptions control over any general statements in the base materials, and the retained-liability carve-outs must be preserved.

Recommended position:
- REJECT the silent reduction of the indemnification cap and RESTORE it to the firm-standard / executed-credit-agreement level (redline Section 8.2).
- CONCEDE (accept) the basket conversion from a deductible to a tipping basket per the controlling client instruction (redline Section 8.3).
- ADD express carve-out language preserving the Schedule 5.2 retained liabilities in all events and excluding them from, and from counting toward, the indemnification basket (redline Section 8.4).

----------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 2: MAE Definition — Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Section reference: Section 2.1 (definition of "Material Adverse Effect"); Schedule 3.7 (pending regulatory inquiries).

Counterparty markup action: The definition of "Material Adverse Effect" adds carve-outs for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.

Playbook requirement: The firm-standard MAE definition contains only narrow carve-outs for regulatory action taken in the ordinary, non-discriminatory course by governmental authorities against the industry generally, and does not excuse adverse events caused by the specific matters under investigation.

Risk rating: HIGH.

Exposure analysis: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries that intersect the markup's MAE carve-outs. If the counterparty's blanket regulatory-action carve-outs are retained, any adverse change, event, or state of facts arising from or relating to those pending inquiries would be excluded from "Material Adverse Effect," thereby eliminating the client's ability to invoke MAE-based protections (e.g., a bring-down condition or termination right) for precisely the regulatory risk present in this deal. The scheduled exceptions (Schedule 3.7) control over the general statements in the base materials, reinforcing that the carve-outs must be narrowed.

Recommended position: REJECT the blanket regulatory-action carve-outs and RESTORE the firm-standard MAE definition, retaining carve-outs only for regulatory actions that (i) are ordinary and non-discriminatory against the industry generally, (ii) do not arise out of the facts or circumstances underlying the two pending inquiries disclosed in Schedule 3.7, and (iii) do not cause a material adverse effect that is the subject of any pending inquiry (redline Section 2.1).

----------------------------------------------------------------------
DEVIATION 3: Survival Period Reduction (Walk-Away Issue)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Section reference: Section 12.3 (Survival of Representations and Warranties); Exhibit B (Survival Matrix).

Counterparty markup action: A new limitation period shortens survival for the core representations.

Playbook requirement: Exhibit B sets the survival matrix for the representations and warranties, including full (non-shortened) survival for the fundamental/core representations, the regulatory-inquiry representations, and the indemnification obligations.

Risk rating: CRITICAL / WALK-AWAY (per controlling client instruction).

Exposure analysis: The counterparty's new limitation period directly contradicts Exhibit B's survival matrix. A shortened survival period would cut off claims for breaches of the core representations — including those relating to the Schedule 3.7 pending regulatory inquiries — well before the risks could mature, stripping the client of a material component of protection. Under the controlling deal-team instruction (doc 110), ANY survival-period reduction is a walk-away issue and is not negotiable.

Recommended position: REJECT the new limitation period and RESTORE the full survival matrix in Exhibit B without any reduction (redline Section 12.3). Flag to the client that this is a walk-away issue consistent with the controlling instruction.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDITIONAL / GENERAL OBSERVATIONS (Missing Protections, Off-Market Terms)
----------------------------------------------------------------------
- Governing law / consent to jurisdiction, control-arrangement (UCC) provisions, and integration clause should be conformed to the depository bank's standard form and executed credit agreement to ensure the agreement operates as a perfected control agreement (redline general insertions).
- Verify that all account details and schedules (Schedule 3.7 and Schedule 5.2) are accurately carried into the final form and that no counterparty revisions undermine the scheduled exceptions, which control over general statements.

III. SUMMARY DEVIATION MATRIX

----------------------------------------------------------------------
| # | Provision      | Counterparty Change          | Playbook / Base Requirement        | Risk Rating        | Recommended Position                |
|---|----------------|------------------------------|------------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------------------------|
| 1 | Sec 8.2 Cap    | Cap silently reduced         | Full firm-standard cap             | HIGH               | REJECT; RESTORE cap                 |
| 1a| Sec 8.3 Basket | Deductible → tipping basket  | Deductible basket                  | MEDIUM (conceded)  | CONCEDE per client instruction      |
| 1b| Sec 5.2 Retained liabilities | Indemnity changes shift retained liabilities | Preserve Schedule 5.2 carve-outs | HIGH | ADD carve-out preservation language |
| 2 | Sec 2.1 MAE    | Blanket regulatory-action carve-outs added | Narrow firm-standard carve-outs; Schedule 3.7 controls | HIGH | REJECT; RESTORE firm-standard MAE   |
| 3 | Sec 12.3 Survival | Survival period shortened  | Full Exhibit B survival matrix      | CRITICAL (walk-away)| REJECT; RESTORE full survival; walk-away issue |
----------------------------------------------------------------------

IV. CONCLUSION AND NEXT STEPS

The counterparty's markup must be returned with (i) the indemnification cap restored, (ii) the MAE regulatory-action carve-outs rejected and replaced with the firm-standard definition preserved against the Schedule 3.7 pending inquiries, and (iii) the survival period restored to the Exhibit B matrix in full — the latter flagged to the client as a walk-away issue under the controlling instruction. The basket conversion is to be conceded. Retained-liability and control-arrangement protections should be confirmed as described above. A tracked-changes redline incorporating these positions accompanies this memorandum (aca-redline.docx).
